scenario_description: A known repository receives separate legal and security observations.
expected: Missing evidence remains unknown and is never silently converted to a passing result.
License evidence identifies both repository and dependency licensing concerns.
Security posture and known vulnerability evidence remain separate observations.
observed: Requested and observed repository identities both equal exact commit 57e89f7223b0960d5ee5ea048c69e3c47e088572; the checkout was clean and its LICENSE Git blob matched GitHub 7d89c6e2d7dea1388df7efe33222068cdd784f8b.

Repository licensing remained Apache-2.0 while 7 of 16 direct dependencies had empty, non-standard, or GPL-family results; all 305 SPDX package licenseDeclared fields remained explicit NOASSERTION rather than passing.

Security posture remained a separate, current repository-level Scorecard not-found observation while OSV-Scanner exited 1 and reported 23 vulnerable package entries, 223 primary advisories, and maximum severity 9.8 across the complete source/lock scope.

PyPI release metadata returned HTTP 200, but both distribution provenance endpoints returned HTTP 404 with zero attestation bundles; the exact GitHub commit signature was valid but was not treated as package provenance.
The three retained artifact hashes and counts matched independent reads; the source checkout stayed clean and no scanner containers remained.
notes: PASS applies only to the acceptance scenario: Blackridge kept legal, posture, known-vulnerability, SBOM, and provenance observations independent and preserved missing evidence as unknown. The PaperQA release candidate itself is BLOCKED pending dependency-license resolution, production-scope vulnerability triage, and release provenance.
